newsitem.title: UK: UK politicians urge closer links in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: UK politicians urge closer links in Latin America.

text.p: British politicians demanded on Wednesday that extra funds be made available to boost the number of diplomats pushing Britain's interests overseas, particularly in the rapidly growing economies of Latin America.

A report by parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee said the flourishing, newly-developed economies in Latin America offered great trade opportunities, adding that a firmer foothold in the continent would "reap vast dividends in the years to come".
It said wholesale cost-cutting in the Foreign Office threatened Britain's ability to forge links abroad.
"The government simply cannot afford to run the Foreign and Commonwealth Office on a shoestring," the committee said.
It added that departmental expenditure should be considered both in terms of the worth of diplomatic, commercial and cultural activity as well as the costs.
"Decisions on the relative weighting of staffing...should be based on detailed analysis and not on which post appears conveniently raidable."
The committee also said the stigma of the past, undemocratic history of regimes in Latin America should be laid aside.

"If the future outlook for Latin America is as rosy as it is painted, the ECGD (Export Credits Guarantee Department) should be encouraged to maximise its business and take a long-term view of the future, rather than being haunted by the ghost of Latin America's past."

The committee said the government's "Link into Latin America" campaign, kicked off in 1995 and aimed at raising the continents profile with British companies, was already paying dividends but policy now had to go further.
